subject: 🤝 Claude Code sessions talk mid-task, catching 89% of bad commands
intro: AI agents are learning to work together. Claude Code sessions now talk to each other mid-task, and its auto mode catches 89% of dangerous commands vs. 13% for tired humans. The solo AI assistant era is quietly ending. Meanwhile, Harvard and MIT just simulated all 8.3 billion humans overnight to test products. Think about that pairing: agents that coordinate autonomously, tested against a synthetic world population. We're not building tools anymore. We're building teams that run without us.

news.headline: Claude Code sessions can now talk to each other mid-task
news.body: Picture this: you have three terminals open on the same project. Backend in one, tests in another, database migration in the third. One session finds a breaking change. You used to manually copy that info across windows. Not anymore. Claude Code now lets sessions talk to each other directly. Here is what it does: Two tools power it under the hood: one finds your active sessions, the other delivers the message. To try it, just update Claude Code to v2.1.224 and say something like "Tell the other session what we just changed." Available on macOS and Linux.
bullets: One session sends a plain-text summary to another, never your full chat history or files
It works both ways: ask another session a question and get the answer back in your active window
Claude can message another session on its own when a change it just made affects what that session is doing
Messages stay local to your machine and never hit Anthropic's servers

news.headline: Anthropic makes Claude Code auto mode default, catching 89% of dangerous commands
news.body: Manual approval for AI shell commands sounds safe. It isn't. In a study with over 1,000 paid testers, humans only caught 13.6% of dangerous commands . After 50 prompts, that dropped to 5%. Approval fatigue is real. Claude Code's auto mode runs a classifier (think: a small AI that checks every action before it runs) on every tool call. It caught 89% of dangerous commands , flat across the whole session. No fatigue. So here's what this opens up: Auto mode becomes the default soon. You'll get an in-app notification. Toggle anytime with Shift+Tab , and admins can pin or disable it in managed settings.
bullets: Kick off multi-hour tasks and walk away, no babysitting permissions
Run multiple tasks in parallel and come back to finished PRs
Classifier tokens no longer count toward your usage limits on Pro, Max, and Team plans

news.headline: OpenAI flags its Astra model as a cybersecurity risk under its safety framework
news.body: OpenAI just hit a milestone nobody was rushing toward. Their upcoming model, Astra , is the first model they've ever flagged as "Critical" for cybersecurity risk. What does Critical actually mean? It means Astra may be able to find and exploit security holes in real-world systems, completely on its own, with zero human help. Think of it like an AI that can independently break into well-protected computer systems just from a high-level instruction. Every previous model, including GPT-5.6 Sol, only hit the "High" tier. Astra is a step above that, which triggers a whole different set of rules under OpenAI's safety playbook. So what's actually happening right now: The goal is still to release Astra broadly, with its cyber powers aimed at defenders, not attackers. But it needs more time to get there safely.
bullets: Internal work on Astra is partially paused until safeguards catch up
Universal monitoring is now active across all uses of the model
Government agencies and safety groups are being brought in to test it
